data.narrative:
Axiom Space, a Series G space-infrastructure company founded by Michael T. Suffredini and Kam Ghaffarian, has raised $350M to date. The Space & Aerospace sector peer universe includes 6 public comps (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers, though neither public nor private comp sets yield sufficient same-stage or valuation-tier alignment for robust median pricing.

Stage-Progression analysis, the sole applicable method, uses $175M (half of total raised) as a base proxy and applies a 1.25x Series G step-up multiplier, yielding $219M. This reflects typical advance to next-stage funding, but relies on an indirect proxy rather than explicit company financials. Public-Comp Anchoring cannot be applied—the Space & Aerospace sector median P/S is 27.4x across the five comparable public tickers, but Axiom's revenue is not disclosed, precluding meaningful revenue-multiple anchoring. Peer-Median triangulation fails due to insufficient narrow-set peers at the same stage and valuation tier.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $186M–$252M, centered on $219M, with $219M as the median point. This range is wide and reflects heavy reliance on stage-progression logic rather than market comparables. Key uncertainties include Axiom's actual revenue run-rate (critical for public-comp validation), the liquidity event timeline, and capital efficiency relative to later-stage peers in commercial space infrastructure.
